arxiv-2101-03441.title: Rate Allocation and Content Placement in Cache Networks
arxiv-2101-03441.creator: Khashayar Kamran, Armin Moharrer, Stratis Ioannidis, and Edmund Yeh
arxiv-2101-03441.description: Abstract We introduce the problem of optimal congestion control in cache networks, whereby both rate allocations and content placements are optimized jointly . We formulate this as a maximization problem with non-convex constraints, and propose solving this problem via (a) a Lagrangian barrier algorithm and (b) a convex relaxation.

arxiv-2205-01066.title: Quantifying Health Inequalities Induced by Data and AI Models
arxiv-2205-01066.creator: Honghan Wu, Minhong Wang, Aneeta Sylolypavan, Sarah Wild
arxiv-2205-01066.description: Abstract AI technologies are being increasingly tested and applied in critical environments including healthcare. Without an effective way to detect and mitigate AI induced inequalities, AI might do more harm than good, potentially leading to the widening of underlying inequalities. This paper proposes a generic allocation-deterioration framework for detecting and quantifying AI induced inequality.

arxiv-2309-03322.title: REBOOT: Reuse Data for Bootstrapping Efficient Real-World Dexterous Manipulation
arxiv-2309-03322.creator: Zheyuan Hu Aaron Rovinsky, Jianlan Luo Vikash Kumar Abhishek Gupta Sergey Levine
arxiv-2309-03322.description: Abstract Dexterous manipulation tasks involving contact-rich interactions pose a significant challenge for both model-based control systems and imitation learning algorithms. The complexity arises from the need for multi-fingered robotic hands to dynamically establish and break contacts, balance non-prehensile forces, and control large degrees of freedom.

arxiv-2310-13321.title: Beyond Hard Samples: Robust and Effective Grammatical Error Correction with Cycle Self-Augmenting
arxiv-2310-13321.creator: Zecheng Tang, Kaiqi Feng, Juntao Li, Min Zhang
arxiv-2310-13321.description: Abstract Recent studies have revealed that grammatical error correction methods in the sequence-to-sequence paradigm are vulnerable to adversarial attack, and simply utilizing adversarial examples in the pre-training or post-training process can significantly enhance the robustness of GEC models to certain types of attack without suffering too much performance loss on clean data.

arxiv-2405-10857.title: Diagnosing and Decoupling the Degradation Mechanisms in Lithium Ion Cells: An Estimation Approach
arxiv-2405-10857.creator: Raja Abhishek Appana, Faissal El Idrissi, Prashanth Ramesh, Marcello Canova, Chun Yong Kang, Kimoon Um
arxiv-2405-10857.description: Abstract Understanding battery degradation in electric vehicles (EVs) under real-world conditions remains a critical yet under-explored area of research. Central to this investigation is the challenge of estimating the specific degradation modes in aged cells with no available information on usage history, bypassing the conventional yet invasive method of tear-down tests.

arxiv-2502-12400.title: Geometric dependence of critical current magnitude and nonreciprocity in planar Josephson junctions
arxiv-2502-12400.creator: William F. Schiela, Melissa Mikalsen, William M. Strickland, Javad Shabani
arxiv-2502-12400.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by William F. Schiela, Melissa Mikalsen, William M. Strickland, Javad Shabani. Planar Josephson junctions in a magnetic field exhibit the superconducting diode effect, by which the critical current magnitude depends on the polarity of the transport current. A number of different mechanisms for the effect have been proposed. Here, we study symmetric, T-shaped planar Josephson junctions with semiconducting weak links in an in-plane magnetic field perpendicular to an applied current bias. arxiv-2506-11874.title: A Short Survey on Formalising Software Requirements with Large Language Models Thanks: Supported by ADAPT research centre, Ireland
arxiv-2506-11874.creator: Arshad Beg, Diarmuid O’Donoghue, Rosemary Monahan
arxiv-2506-11874.description: Abstract This paper presents a focused literature survey on the use of large language models (LLM) to assist in writing formal specifications for software. A summary of thirty-five key papers is presented, including examples for specifying programs written in Dafny, C and Java.

arxiv-2511-01800.title: Bayesian Coreset Optimization for Personalized Federated Learning
arxiv-2511-01800.creator: Prateek Chanda, Shrey Modi, Ganesh Ramakrishnan
arxiv-2511-01800.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Prateek Chanda, Shrey Modi, Ganesh Ramakrishnan. In a distributed machine learning setting like Federated Learning where there are multiple clients involved which update their individual weights to a single central server, often training on the entire individual client’s dataset for each client becomes cumbersome.

arxiv-2511-08379.title: SOM Directions are Better than One: Multi-Directional Refusal Suppression in Language Models
arxiv-2511-08379.creator: Giorgio Piras, Raffaele Mura, Fabio Brau, Luca Oneto, Fabio Roli, Battista Biggio
arxiv-2511-08379.description: Abstract Refusal refers to the functional behavior enabling safety-aligned language models to reject harmful or unethical prompts. Following the growing scientific interest in mechanistic interpretability, recent work encoded refusal behavior as a single direction in the model’s latent space; e.g., computed as the difference between the centroids of harmful and harmless prompt representations.

arxiv-2601-14532.title: Search over Self-Edit Strategies for LLM Adaptation
arxiv-2601-14532.creator: Alistair Cheong, Haolin Cong, Tyler Yang, Dustin Miao
arxiv-2601-14532.description: Abstract Many LLM-based open-ended search systems freeze the foundation model that proposes improvements to existing solutions, which may bottleneck long-run progress. Recent work has explored updating the proposal model at test time [ 11 ] , but the update strategy is still typically hand-specified.

pmc-10669083.title: Risk Factors for CMV and BK Infections in an Elderly Veteran Population Following Kidney Transplantation: Implications for Immunosuppression Induction and Management
pmc-10669083.creator: Anne Thorndyke, Cara Joyce, Manpreet Samra, Laura Cotiguala, Christine Trotter, Oswaldo Aguirre, W James Chon, Rupinder Sodhi, Reynold I Lopez-Soler, Adriana Pistol
pmc-10669083.description: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) and BK Polyomavirus (BKPyV) are the most common opportunistic pathogens following kidney transplantation. We evaluated 102 patients with a median age of 63 at Edward Hines VA Hospital from November 2020 to December 2022. Our primary interest was the incidence of CMV and BKPyV infections, as well as CMV and BKPyV coinfection.

pmc-10728793.title: The Effectiveness of Publicly Available Web-Based Interventions in Promoting Health App Use, Digital Health Literacy, and Media Literacy: Pre-Post Evaluation Study
pmc-10728793.creator: Lars König, Ralf Suhr
pmc-10728793.description: BackgroundAccording to the World Health Organization, implementing mobile health (mHealth) technologies can increase access to quality health services worldwide. mHealth apps for smartphones, also known as health apps, are a central component of mHealth, and they are already used in diverse medical contexts.

pmc-11585531.title: Transcriptomic, mutational and structural bioinformatics approaches to explore the therapeutic role of FAP in predominant cancer types
pmc-11585531.creator: Gayathri Ashok, Abdullah F. AlAsmari, Fawaz AlAsmari, Paul Livingstone, Anand Anbarasu, Sudha Ramaiah
pmc-11585531.description: Fibroblast activating protein (FAP) is a cell surface marker of cancer-associated fibroblasts with a distinct pro-tumorigenic role. The present study analyzed the pan-cancer expression; and clinical and mutational profiles of the FAP coding gene. Molecular dynamics simulation (MDS) deciphered the backbone dynamics and energetics of FAP.

pmc-12451325.title: Consensus-based research priorities for post-collision care in the Western Cape province of South Africa
pmc-12451325.creator: Naseef Abdullah, Tim Nutbeam, Colleen J. Saunders, Craig Wylie, Nigel Lang, Willem Stassen
pmc-12451325.description: IntroductionRoad traffic injuries constitute a significant global health burden, causing 1.3 million deaths and 50 million injuries annually, with 92 % of fatalities occurring in low-and middle-income countries (LMICs). Despite this disproportionate impact, research priorities in post-collision care often reflect high-income country contexts, creating a critical misalignment between evidence generation and contextual realities in LMICs.

pmc-12505639.title: Cytometric and genetic analysis of Slovenian local apple genotypes
pmc-12505639.creator: Kristina Gostinčar, Gregor Osterc, Nataša Štajner, Zlata Luthar
pmc-12505639.description: BackgroundThe genetic diversity and ploidy of apple varieties in Slovenia is not well known so far. In this study, a total of 233 genotypes and 8 reference varieties were analysed with a set of 15 SSR markers in order to estimate the genetic diversity and to determine the genetic structure and relationships among the apple germplasm studied.

pmc-12569426.title: Prevention of Unbearable Situations and Harms Protocol: A Quality Improvement Initiative in Neurological Delirium
pmc-12569426.creator: Mi Sun Kim, Sungyang Jo, Hyung Ja Kim, Sun Young Pyun, Seonok Kim, Sun Mae Park, Yong Seo Koo
pmc-12569426.description: Background and PurposeHyperactive delirium in neurological wards frequently results in patient harm, falls, device removal, and caregiver injuries, alongside significant staff burnout. To address inconsistent management practices, we developed the Prevention of Unbearable Situations and Harms (PUSH) protocol, a structured multidisciplinary approach to proactively manage hyperactive delirium.
